Headquarters: San Francisco, CA, New York, NY, Portland, OR, or Remote within Canada or United States

About the Role

Mercury is seeking a Business Continuity Management (BCM) Lead to build and lead an enterprise-wide continuity program as we prepare to become a bank. As part of the Risk team, this leader will establish practical standards, clear accountability, and tested capabilities to maintain critical services and recover effectively from disruptions, with direct visibility to the CRO and senior leadership.

This role fills the need for a dedicated leader to coordinate BCM across the organization. The ideal candidate combines deep continuity and resilience expertise with the judgment to build a proportionate program in a fast-moving environment, working effectively with Engineering, Operations, Product, Information Security, Legal, Compliance, and business teams.

The BCM Lead will own the enterprise framework, coordination, oversight, and reporting. Business and technology owners will remain accountable for their continuity plans and recovery execution.Because this is a new program, the Lead will be hands-on in the initial build: facilitating the first round of BIAs and plans side by side with owners, running exercises, and driving identified gaps through remediation. This leader will also work closely with Engineering on technology disaster recovery and with relevant teams on incident response, crisis management, and third-party resilience.

Key Responsibilities

• Develop and implement Mercury’s enterprise BCM framework, policies, standards, governance, and operating model, with a prioritized implementation roadmap aligned to bank-launch readiness and critical services.

• Partner with business owners to identify critical services, conduct business impact analyses (customer, financial, operational, and regulatory), and map dependencies across people, processes, technology, facilities, and third parties, including single points of failure.

• Establish recovery time objectives (RTOs) and recovery point objectives (RPOs), where applicable, with business and technology owners; challenge gaps between objectives and recovery capabilities.

• Set standards for continuity plans and recovery procedures, and facilitate and support accountable owners in developing actionable plans and alternative operating arrangements.

• Coordinate business continuity with technology disaster recovery, incident response, and crisis management, with clear activation criteria, escalation paths, and communications responsibilities.

• Design and lead a risk-based exercise program, from tabletop simulations to end-to-end recovery tests, and drive lessons learned, remediation tracking, and verification that gaps are closed.

• Partner with Third-Party Risk Management and vendor owners to assess critical provider recovery capabilities, contingency arrangements, and concentration dependencies.

• Embed continuity considerations into new products, material business changes, and technology implementations.

• Establish metrics and reporting that give management and relevant committees visibility into readiness, testing outcomes, material gaps, and overdue remediation.

• Build and lead a growing BCM team, including hiring and developing analysts as the program scales over the next year.

• Deliver role-based training and promote awareness of continuity responsibilities across the organization.

• Support regulatory examinations and bank-launch readiness reviews with accurate documentation and evidence of recovery capability.

Qualifications

• 10+ years of experience in business continuity management, operational resilience, disaster recovery, or a related discipline within a fintech, financial institution, technology company, or other highly regulated environment.

• Demonstrated experience building or materially enhancing an enterprise BCM program, including governance, implementation, testing, and reporting.

• Strong skills in business impact analysis, critical-service identification, dependency mapping, and recovery objective development.

• Experience developing actionable continuity plans and leading exercises that test recovery assumptions and expose gaps.

• Sufficient technical fluency to work with Engineering on cloud services, system dependencies, data recovery, and technology disaster recovery.

• Working knowledge of third-party risk management, including assessing critical vendor recovery capabilities, contingency arrangements and concentration risk.

• Proven ability to drive cross-functional remediation through influence, with a clear view of where BCM oversight ends and business or technology ownership begins.

• Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain readiness gaps and tradeoffs to senior leadership.

• Experience managing a team of Business Continuity analysts.

Preferred Qualifications

• Familiarity with banking supervisory expectations for business continuity, and operational resilience.

• Experience operating in a company-building or bank-building environment.

• Familiarity with recognized continuity standards, such as ISO 22301, and BCM tools for plan management, exercises, and issue tracking.

• Relevant professional certification, such as CBCP or MBCI.

Leadership Attributes

• Pragmatic, first-principles builder who turns ambiguous needs into clear priorities and designs a program that fits Mercury’s operations and scale.

• Takes ownership and follows through from identified gaps to demonstrated recovery.

• Collaborative, low-ego, and effective across the three lines of defense.

• Calm under pressure and able to facilitate clear decisions during disruptions.

• Able to challenge constructively, distinguish material gaps from theoretical concerns, and avoid over-engineering.

*Mercury is a fintech company, not an FDIC-insured bank. Banking services provided through Choice Financial Group and Column N.A., Members FDIC.

Mercury values diversity & belonging and is proud to be an Equal Employment Opportunity employer. All individuals seeking employment at Mercury are considered without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, age, sex, marital status, ancestry, physical or mental disability, veteran status, gender identity, sexual orientation, or any other legally protected characteristic. Role: Senior Staff Product Designer, AI | Deel
Company: Deel
Location: Fully remote
Job type: Full-time

About Deel
Deel is an all-in-one payroll and HR platform for global teams. It covers HRIS, payroll, compliance, benefits and equipment for every type of worker in 150+ countries. About 7,000 people work there, across more than 100 countries and 74 languages. Deel reached $1B in annual revenue in just over five years and is valued at $17.3B. It’s pre-IPO, and AI is at the centre of where it’s heading next.
About the role
You’ll lead design for Deel’s AI products: Deel AI, Akai, chat interfaces, agents and developer tools. AI touches every part of Deel, so the job has two halves. You’ll design the core AI experiences yourself, and you’ll help other teams bring AI into their own products. You’ll work closely with the Principal Designer, who owns the intent bar and the intelligent OS layer. Together you’ll make Deel feel like one connected, intelligent system.
What you’ll do
• 
Set the design direction for how AI shows up across the platform: in-chat actions, agent workflows, proactive notifications, anomaly detection and human-in-the-loop moments.
• 
Turn good AI design into clear standards and reusable patterns, together with the design system team.
• 
Help other teams work out where AI fits in their area. You’ll do the work and show them how.
• 
Build the habits that keep quality high: user research, competitor analysis and regular dogfooding of AI products.
• 
Move quickly between topics and make decisions on your own. You’ll work with people across the company, from US sales to risk and compliance.
• 
Mentor designers and help the AI design practice grow.
What you need to succeed
• 
8+ years in product design, including 3+ at Staff level or above.
• 
Deep experience designing AI products such as conversational UX, agents, copilots and automation. Ideally, you’ve taken something from zero to one and then scaled it.
• 
At least one AI feature you shipped inside a product with a proven result, and you can walk us through the whole story: the problem, the research, the prototype, the launch and the outcome.
• 
Excellent craft, and a portfolio that makes people say “wow”. It needs at least one case study.
• 
AI is the first tool you reach for, before Figma or a doc. You follow new releases and actually use them in your work.
• 
You think in systems, and you’re comfortable working with ML engineers on error states and confidence thresholds.
• 
You enjoy moving fast and don’t mind figuring things out as you go.
Nice to have
• 
You can ship your own work to production.
• 
Experience applying behavioural science to AI products.
• 
A background in payroll, HR, fintech or compliance, or personal projects you’re proud of.
What you get
• 
The chance to shape how AI works across a pre-IPO global platform, with stock grants depending on your role and location.
• 
Fully remote, async-friendly work, plus an optional flexible office membership with IWG.
• 
A strong design team to learn from, and a clear career ladder.
• 
Fair pay based on your skills and experience. Deel never asks about your salary history.

Headquarters: Remote, United States

Principal Product Manager, Agentic AI

REMOTE, United States

JOB OVERVIEW

Legion is building AI agents that carry out workforce management work, not agents that describe it.

Much of what is presented as AI in workforce management today is a conversational layer over an existing scheduling screen. The more substantial problem — software that reasons over demand, labor regulation, and employee preferences, then acts, with a person in the loop wherever the stakes require one — remains unsolved across the category. Legion intends to solve it, and this role leads the product work to get there.

You will take an agent surface from operational research through specification, prototype, evaluation, and enterprise deployment, working hands-on throughout. You will work closely with Legion's AI Lab engineers and with our CEO, who is engaged in this work daily.

RESPONSIBILITIES AND DUTIES

Agent definition. Determine what an agent is responsible for, which tools it may call, what it must escalate, what it must never do, and what a manager sees when it acts. These decisions affect employee pay and legal compliance. Much of this work is pre-launch, so you will shape the direction rather than inherit it. 

Problem selection. The hardest judgment in agentic product work is identifying which workflows suit an agent and which do not. You will spend substantial time inside customer operations — district managers, store managers, labor operations, frontline employees — and return with a ranked, defensible view of where an agent creates measurable value and where it does not.

The human-in-the-loop contract. Scheduling decisions affect income, childcare arrangements, and legal protections. For each agent action you will define where autonomy is appropriate, the escalation thresholds, how a manager overrides the system, what is logged, and how a compliance team audits the outcome. Legion treats this as a first-class design problem.

Build quality. You are accountable for what ships, not for what was specified. That means staying engaged through implementation: reviewing the build against the specification as it comes together, using the product yourself before anyone else is asked to, joining bug triage and design review, catching drift from intent while it is still cheap to correct, and holding a release when the quality is not there. Our customers experience the build, not the document. A well-written specification that produced a product managers do not trust is failed product work, and we assess it that way.

Evaluation. Build and maintain the evaluation sets that determine whether an agent is ready to ship and whether it is degrading in production — writing the cases, reviewing failure traces, setting the pass criteria. You will be the person who holds a release when the demonstration is persuasive and the evaluation is not.

Specifications. Legion uses Functional Requirements Documents as its ground-truth specification layer; release notes, enablement material, and sales content are generated from maintained specifications rather than reconstructed from code or institutional memory. Write FRDs that meet that standard and keep them accurate after release. A specification is where the work begins, not where your responsibility ends.

Commercialization. Partner with go-to-market on packaging, metering, pricing inputs, and field readiness. Agentic products raise difficult commercial questions — what unit to meter, what a customer is paying for when software performs work a person previously did — and you will be expected to hold a considered position on them.

Design-partner delivery. Lead agent deployments with large enterprise design partners: scoping the pilot, establishing success criteria before it begins, joining failure reviews, and determining what becomes generally available and what remains bespoke.

TECHNICAL EXPECTATIONS

Legion is looking for a product manager who builds, rather than one who directs others who build. In a typical week, this role involves:

• Writing and iterating on prompts and system prompts directly, and explaining why a change improved a behavior

• Standing up a working prototype of a proposed agent — tool definitions, structured outputs, retries, guardrails — before engineering is asked to build anything

• Using agentic coding tools (Claude Code or equivalent) daily: prototyping, data analysis, specification work, and reading the codebase behind your specifications

• Reviewing an execution trace and diagnosing whether a failure originates in a tool description, a retrieval gap, a context-window constraint, an under-specified output schema, or a genuine model limitation

• Building and running evaluation sets, and interpreting the results without a data scientist to translate them

• Holding an informed position on retrieval design, tool-use patterns, structured output, model routing, latency and cost trade-offs, and multi-tenant safety in enterprise SaaS

• Opening pull requests against our codebase — a prototype, a prompt change, an evaluation fixture, a specification stub. Pushing code is permitted and actively encouraged for product managers who want to work that way. It is not a requirement of the role, and the same review standards apply to everyone.

• Following model releases, agent frameworks, and protocol changes, and translating them into roadmap implications within days rather than quarters

We recognize that this is a demanding technical bar for a product role. It reflects what the work actually requires.

REQUIRED SKILLS AND QUALIFICATIONS

• 7+ years in product management (Senior) or 10+ years (Principal), including at least 2 years shipping LLM-backed features to external, paying users — not internal tools, proofs of concept, or hackathon projects

• Demonstrated hands-on capability of the kind described above. Expect to show your work.

• Substantial enterprise B2B SaaS experience: multi-tenant architecture, role-based access control, audit trails, single sign-on, data residency, security review, and enterprise procurement. You should be able to anticipate what a customer's security questionnaire will ask about an LLM feature.

• A record of taking an ambiguous, operationally complex domain problem through to a shipped product with demonstrated adoption — not only launch

• Evidence of staying with a product through implementation and owning its quality at release. We will ask about a release you delayed or stopped, what you found, and how you found it.

• The judgment to recognize what current models cannot do reliably, and the willingness to say so when a room expects a different answer

• Comfort working inside a codebase. An engineering background is not required, but you should be able to read the code behind what you are specifying, run it locally, and open a pull request.

• Strong written communication. Legion runs on documents, and candidates are evaluated substantially on how they write.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS AND ATTRIBUTES

• Direct experience in workforce management, HCM, ERP, supply chain, or another operationally complex enterprise domain with compliance exposure

• Familiarity with labor compliance regimes — predictive scheduling ordinances, meal and rest break rules, union work rules — or demonstrated ability to become fluent in a comparable regulatory domain quickly

• Background in demand forecasting, optimization, or decision systems

• Experience building platform or authoring surfaces that customers configure themselves

• An engineering or technical degree, or prior experience as an engineer or data scientist

• Experience with products sold into frontline-heavy industries: retail, hospitality, healthcare, or manufacturing

SCOPE OF ROLE, STATED PLAINLY

So that candidates can assess fit early:

• This is an individual contributor role. There is no team to inherit and no management responsibility at present.

Job Level: Analyst (Professional):

Company Profile

Morgan Stanley is a leading global financial services firm providing a wide range of investment banking, securities, investment management and wealth management services. The Firm's employees serve clients worldwide including corporations, governments and individuals from more than 1,200 offices in 43 countries.

As a market leader, the talent and passion of our people is critical to our success. Together, we share a common set of values rooted in integrity, excellence and strong team ethic. Morgan Stanley can provide a superior foundation for building a professional career - a place for people to learn, to achieve and grow. A philosophy that balances personal lifestyles, perspectives and needs is an important part of our culture.

Department Profile

Morgan Stanley is a worldwide leader in investment banking and is one of the top firms in mergers and acquisitions, underwriting of equity and equity-related transactions, corporate debt issuance, and high-yield debt financing. With professionals in 30 countries, we are consistently recognized for our performance in both traditional and innovative financing techniques, helping a wide range of clients around the world to make and execute decisions about their business strategy and financial structure.

We are looking for an Investment Banking / Global Capital Markets professional to join our Global Centers in Mumbai. The successful candidate will play a key role in providing deal execution support, preparing marketing materials including pitchbooks, conducting research and analytics, and providing internal process support to coverage and product teams across Equity Capital Markets, Debt Capital Markets and Mergers and Acquisitions globally.

You will receive variety of trainings covering financial analysis, business presentations, and practical skills. At the end of training, you will be able to understand financial concepts and have a strong understanding of the Morgan Stanley culture. In this role, you will gain exposure to financial markets and macro trends, build knowledge of banking and capital markets sectors and products, and work with bankers in core locations. High performers will be eligible for internal mobility opportunities globally.

Key Responsibilities

• Presentations, Analyst presentations and company profiles among others
• Perform financial analysis, including financial metric benchmarking, capital structure analysis, firepower analysis and its interpretation
• Perform company valuation including developing financial models and relative valuation
• Gather and synthesize financial and operating information about companies, industries and governments to analyze performance and drive strategic client dialogue
• Develop industry / macro market landscape including key themes / trends, economic indicators, competitive landscape among other items
• Maintain and update databases leveraged by senior management and deal teams
• Generate presentations and memoranda for a wider senior audience within the Firm
• Other administrative tasks to support overall deal flow and business

Skills And Qualifications

• MBA / CA / Bachelor’s Degree or equivalent
• 1 – 3 years of work experience in related field
• Keen interest in corporate finance / capital markets
• Written competency and spoken language fluency in English
• Good communication and interpersonal skills to collaborate effectively with global teams
• Strong analytical and numerical skills and are at ease with financial data
• Agility and ability to multi-task and thrive in a fast-paced environment
• Team player with a strong work ethic and motivation to learn
• Ability to manage expectations and handle high-pressure situations
• Must have an intermediate skill level in Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint
